title: Luck and Predictability in the Life Course
abstract: There is an emerging recognition among sociological theorists that luck may play a substantial role in life course achievement. There is also a nascent empirical literature that finds life outcomes to be unpredictable and unexpected life events to be a likely cause. A third literature of causal event studies provides thousands of point estimates of the life course consequences of random events. This review brings these literatures together under a unified framework.
authors_text: van de Rijt, Arnout; Bernardi, Fabrizio; Foley, William; Sage, Lucas
